original_question: Let f(x) be a polynomial in C[x] with exactly k monomials. Does there exist a number N(k) such that if the first N(k) moments M_n = integral_0^1 f(x)^n dx vanish for 1 <= n <= N(k), then f must be zero; and if such a number exists, determine N(k) or give a good upper bound for it.
target_in_paper: Problem 27(i)-(ii) in Section 7.1 ("A moments problem"), which is the one-variable fewnomial finite-moment variant of the broader multivariable moments question posed just before it in Problem 26.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's actual target almost verbatim: it is the one-variable complex-polynomial version, it counts monomials via a parameter k, it asks whether vanishing of the initial moments M_n = ∫_0^1 f(x)^n dx up to some bound N(k) forces f to be zero, and it includes the second part asking to determine N(k) or give a good upper bound.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is Problem 27 in Section 7.1, not the broader Problem 26; Problem 26 is the multivariable infinite-moment question, while Problem 27 is the related one-variable finite-moment/fewnomial version.
The ambient ring is explicitly C[x], i.e. one-variable polynomials with complex coefficients.
To make the monomial count fully stand-alone, it is best to say that f has exactly k nonzero monomial terms in its standard expansion.
The quantifier on N(k) is that it depends only on k, not on the particular polynomial f.
The moment conditions are exactly M_n = ∫_0^1 f(x)^n dx = 0 for every integer n with 1 ≤ n ≤ N(k).
The conclusion should be stated as f = 0, meaning the zero polynomial.
There are no additional degree bounds, weight functions, or coefficient restrictions in the paper's formulation.
No explicit equivalent reformulation is provided for Problem 27 itself; the nearby equivalence in Section 7.1 applies only to Problem 26 in the special case n = 1.
refined_question:
For a given integer k ≥ 1, let f(x) ∈ C[x] be a one-variable polynomial with exactly k nonzero monomial terms. Does there exist an integer N(k), depending only on k, such that if
M_n := ∫_0^1 f(x)^n dx = 0 for every n = 1, 2, ..., N(k),
then f must be the zero polynomial? If such an N(k) exists, determine N(k) or at least give a good upper bound for it.
justification: The draft is aimed at Problem 27, not at a broader neighboring problem. In Section 7.1 the paper first states Problem 26 for a general polynomial f(x_1, ..., x_n) ∈ C[x_1, ..., x_n] with all moments vanishing, and then introduces Problem 27 as an 'interesting related question' specialized to one variable, finitely many initial moments, and a bound depending on the number k of monomials. The wording of your draft tracks Problem 27(i)-(ii) very closely. The only refinements needed are to make explicit that the setting is C[x], that k counts nonzero monomial terms, and that N(k) is universal for all such f with k monomials. Because the paper does not prove an equivalent reformulation for Problem 27 itself, the refined question should stay in this exact moment-vanishing form rather than importing the separate equivalence stated for Problem 26 when n = 1.
